# AI / LLM Integration

Reference file for [citations.md](../citations.md).

## Overview

Windmill has native AI agent steps as first-class flow components [15] and
provides an MCP server for LLM clients to interact with Windmill [14].
However, for the PA use case (LLM is the orchestrator, engine runs
deterministic pipelines), the AI integration is nice-to-have — the critical
capability is CLI execution [5].

## MCP Server

Windmill exposes an MCP server using HTTP streamable transport [14].

### Authentication

| Method | URL Pattern | Source |
|--------|-------------|--------|
| OAuth | `<base_url>/api/mcp/gateway` | [14] |
| Token | `<base_url>/api/mcp/w/<workspace-id>/mcp?token=<token>` | [14] |

### Exposed Tools (40+)

| Category | Examples | Source |
|----------|----------|--------|
| Scripts | listScripts, runScriptByPath | [14] |
| Flows | listFlows, runFlowByPath | [14] |
| Resources | listResource, createResource | [14] |
| Jobs | listJobs (monitoring) | [14] |
| Schedules | listSchedules | [14] |
| Workers | listWorkers | [14] |
| Docs | queryDocumentation (EE only) | [14] |

### Compatible Clients

- Claude Desktop (Settings > Integrations)
- Cursor (Settings > MCP Tools)
- Claude Code CLI (`claude mcp add`)
- Any MCP client supporting HTTP streamable transport

Source: [14]

### Limitation

The MCP integration is one-directional: Windmill exposes itself as an MCP
server for external LLM clients. There is no documented mechanism for
Windmill flows to consume external MCP servers [14].

**Exception:** AI agent steps within flows can connect to external MCP
servers (HTTP streamable only) [15].

### Features

| Feature | Details | Source |
|---------|---------|--------|
| Structured output | JSON schema for response formatting | [15] |
| Tool integration | Inline scripts, workspace scripts, Hub scripts | [15] |
| Web search | Native via OpenAI/Anthropic/Google providers | [15] |

| Memory | Auto or manual, OpenAI message format | [15] |

| Image support | Input and output | [15] |
| Chat mode | Conversational UI from flows | [15] |
| Prompt caching | Automatic for Anthropic | [15] |

### Output Structure

Returns an object with [15]:
- `output`: Final AI response (text, array, or structured JSON)
- `messages`: Complete conversation history
- `usage`: Token metrics (input, output, total, cache tokens)
- `wm_stream`: Full streaming record (streaming mode only)

## Comparison to n8n AI Integration

| Aspect | Windmill | n8n |
|--------|----------|-----|
| AI node count | Native agent steps | 70+ LangChain nodes [n8n research] |
| Framework | Native implementation | LangChain JavaScript |
| MCP support | Server + client (in agents) | MCP Client tool |
| LLM providers | 10+ | 11+ |
| Vector stores | Not native | 12+ (Pinecone, Qdrant, etc.) |
| RAG | Via scripts | Native nodes |
| Memory | Auto/manual | 8+ memory node types |
| Agent nesting | 2 levels | Via sub-workflow |

n8n has a deeper AI integration ecosystem (70+ nodes, vector stores, RAG
pipelines). Windmill's AI steps are simpler but functional for basic agent
workflows [15].

## Relevance to PA Use Case

For the personal assistant use case:
- **MCP server is the key feature** — the PA (Claude Code) can use Windmill's
  MCP server to list, trigger, and monitor workflows directly
- AI agent steps are secondary — the PA is already the LLM layer
- The MCP integration means the PA doesn't need to use raw REST API calls;
  it can interact via the MCP protocol natively

## Gaps and Limitations

- No native vector store integration (use scripts)
- No native RAG pipeline (use scripts/flows)
- AI agent steps limited to 2 nesting levels [15]
- Only HTTP streamable MCP servers supported [15]
- queryDocumentation MCP tool is EE-only [14]
